audit_status.source_base: Greek 1 Corinthians text tradition, draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed for wilderness warnings, temptation, cup/table participation, idol table, liberty and conscience, do all to Divine glory.

verses.restored: For I do not want you to be unaware, siblings, that our fathers were all under the cloud and all passed through the sea,

familiar.text: Moreover, brethren, I would not that ye should be ignorant, how that all our fathers were under the cloud, and all passed through the sea;

modern.text: I do not want you to be unaware, brothers, that our forefathers were all under the cloud, and that they all passed through the sea.

original.text: Οὐ θέλω ⸀γὰρ ὑμᾶς ἀγνοεῖν, ἀδελφοί, ὅτι οἱ πατέρες ἡμῶν πάντες ὑπὸ τὴν νεφέλην ἦσαν καὶ πάντες διὰ τῆς θαλάσσης διῆλθον,

verses.restored: and all were baptized into Moses in the cloud and in the sea,

familiar.text: And were all baptized unto Moses in the cloud and in the sea;

modern.text: They were all baptized into Moses in the cloud and in the sea.

original.text: καὶ πάντες εἰς τὸν Μωϋσῆν ⸀ἐβαπτίσαντο ἐν τῇ νεφέλῃ καὶ ἐν τῇ θαλάσσῃ,

verses.restored: and all ate the same spiritual food,

familiar.text: And did all eat the same spiritual meat;

modern.text: They all ate the same spiritual food

original.text: καὶ πάντες τὸ αὐτὸ ⸂πνευματικὸν βρῶμα⸃ ἔφαγον

verses.restored: and all drank the same spiritual drink; for they were drinking from the spiritual rock following them, and the rock was Messiah.

familiar.text: And did all drink the same spiritual drink: for they drank of that spiritual Rock that followed them: and that Rock was Christ.

modern.text: and drank the same spiritual drink; for they drank from the spiritual rock that accompanied them, and that rock was Christ.

original.text: καὶ πάντες τὸ αὐτὸ ⸂πνευματικὸν ἔπιον πόμα⸃, ἔπινον γὰρ ἐκ πνευματικῆς ἀκολουθούσης πέτρας, ἡ ⸂πέτρα δὲ⸃ ἦν ὁ Χριστός·

verses.restored: Nevertheless, with most of them the Divine was not pleased, for they were scattered in the wilderness.

familiar.text: But with many of them God was not well pleased: for they were overthrown in the wilderness.

modern.text: Nevertheless, God was not pleased with most of them, for they were struck down in the wilderness.

original.text: ἀλλʼ οὐκ ἐν τοῖς πλείοσιν αὐτῶν ηὐδόκησεν ὁ θεός, κατεστρώθησαν γὰρ ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ.

verses.restored: These things became patterns for us, so that we would not be desirers of harmful things, just as they also desired.

familiar.text: Now these things were our examples, to the intent we should not lust after evil things, as they also lusted.

modern.text: These things took place as examples to keep us from craving evil things as they did.

original.text: Ταῦτα δὲ τύποι ἡμῶν ἐγενήθησαν, εἰς τὸ μὴ εἶναι ἡμᾶς ἐπιθυμητὰς κακῶν, καθὼς κἀκεῖνοι ἐπεθύμησαν.

verses.restored: Do not become idolaters, as some of them; just as it is written: The people sat down to eat and drink and rose up to play.

familiar.text: Neither be ye idolaters, as were some of them; as it is written, The people sat down to eat and drink, and rose up to play.

modern.text: Do not be idolaters, as some of them were. As it is written: “The people sat down to eat and to drink, and got up to indulge in revelry.”

original.text: μηδὲ εἰδωλολάτραι γίνεσθε, καθώς τινες αὐτῶν· ὥσπερ γέγραπται· Ἐκάθισεν ὁ λαὸς φαγεῖν καὶ πεῖν, καὶ ἀνέστησαν παίζειν.

verses.restored: Nor should we practice sexual immorality/misuse, as some of them practiced, and twenty-three thousand fell in one day.

familiar.text: Neither let us commit fornication, as some of them committed, and fell in one day three and twenty thousand.

modern.text: We should not commit sexual immorality, as some of them did, and in one day twenty-three thousand of them died.

original.text: μηδὲ πορνεύωμεν, καθώς τινες αὐτῶν ἐπόρνευσαν, καὶ ἔπεσαν μιᾷ ἡμέρᾳ εἴκοσι τρεῖς χιλιάδες.

verses.restored: Nor should we test Messiah, as some of them tested, and were destroyed by serpents.

familiar.text: Neither let us tempt Christ, as some of them also tempted, and were destroyed of serpents.

modern.text: We should not test Christ, as some of them did, and were killed by snakes.

original.text: μηδὲ ἐκπειράζωμεν τὸν ⸀Χριστόν, ⸀καθώς τινες αὐτῶν ἐπείρασαν, καὶ ὑπὸ τῶν ὄφεων ⸀ἀπώλλυντο.

verses.restored: Nor grumble, as some of them grumbled, and were destroyed by the destroyer.

familiar.text: Neither murmur ye, as some of them also murmured, and were destroyed of the destroyer.

modern.text: And do not complain, as some of them did, and were killed by the destroying angel.

original.text: μηδὲ γογγύζετε, ⸀καθάπερ τινὲς αὐτῶν ἐγόγγυσαν, καὶ ἀπώλοντο ὑπὸ τοῦ ὀλοθρευτοῦ.

verses.restored: These things happened to them as patterns, and were written for our admonition, upon whom the completions of the ages have come.

familiar.text: Now all these things happened unto them for ensamples: and they are written for our admonition, upon whom the ends of the world are come.

modern.text: Now these things happened to them as examples and were written down as warnings for us, on whom the fulfillment of the ages has come.

original.text: ταῦτα ⸀δὲ ⸂τυπικῶς συνέβαινεν⸃ ἐκείνοις, ἐγράφη δὲ πρὸς νουθεσίαν ἡμῶν, εἰς οὓς τὰ τέλη τῶν αἰώνων ⸀κατήντηκεν.

verses.restored: Therefore let the one thinking to stand watch lest one fall.

familiar.text: Wherefore let him that thinketh he standeth take heed lest he fall.

modern.text: So the one who thinks he is standing firm should be careful not to fall.

original.text: ὥστε ὁ δοκῶν ἑστάναι βλεπέτω μὴ πέσῃ,

verses.restored: No testing has taken you except what is human; but trustworthy is the Divine, who will not allow you to be tested beyond what you are able, but with the testing will also make the way out, so that you may be able to bear it.

familiar.text: There hath no temptation taken you but such as is common to man: but God is faithful, who will not suffer you to be tempted above that ye are able; but will with the temptation also make a way to escape, that ye may be able to bear it.

modern.text: No temptation has seized you except what is common to man. And God is faithful; He will not let you be tempted beyond what you can bear. But when you are tempted, He will also provide an escape, so that you can stand up under it. Flee from Idolatry (Exodus 20:22–26)

original.text: πειρασμὸς ὑμᾶς οὐκ εἴληφεν εἰ μὴ ἀνθρώπινος· πιστὸς δὲ ὁ θεός, ὃς οὐκ ἐάσει ὑμᾶς πειρασθῆναι ὑπὲρ ὃ δύνασθε, ἀλλὰ ποιήσει σὺν τῷ πειρασμῷ καὶ τὴν ἔκβασιν τοῦ ⸀δύνασθαι ὑπενεγκεῖν.

verses.restored: Therefore, my beloved, flee from idolatry.

familiar.text: Wherefore, my dearly beloved, flee from idolatry.

modern.text: Therefore, my beloved, flee from idolatry.

original.text: Διόπερ, ἀγαπητοί μου, φεύγετε ἀπὸ τῆς εἰδωλολατρίας.

verses.restored: I speak as to discerning ones; judge what I say.

familiar.text: I speak as to wise men; judge ye what I say.

modern.text: I speak to reasonable people; judge for yourselves what I say.

original.text: ὡς φρονίμοις λέγω· κρίνατε ὑμεῖς ὅ φημι.

verses.restored: The cup of blessing that we bless, is it not fellowship/participation of the blood of Messiah? The bread that we break, is it not fellowship/participation of the body of Messiah?

familiar.text: The cup of blessing which we bless, is it not the communion of the blood of Christ? The bread which we break, is it not the communion of the body of Christ?

modern.text: Is not the cup of blessing that we bless a participation in the blood of Christ? And is not the bread that we break a participation in the body of Christ?

original.text: τὸ ποτήριον τῆς εὐλογίας ὃ εὐλογοῦμεν, οὐχὶ κοινωνία ⸂ἐστὶν τοῦ αἵματος τοῦ Χριστοῦ⸃; τὸν ἄρτον ὃν κλῶμεν, οὐχὶ κοινωνία τοῦ σώματος τοῦ Χριστοῦ ἐστιν;

verses.restored: Because there is one bread, we the many are one body, for we all share from the one bread.

familiar.text: For we being many are one bread, and one body: for we are all partakers of that one bread.

modern.text: Because there is one loaf, we who are many are one body; for we all partake of the one loaf.

original.text: ὅτι εἷς ἄρτος, ἓν σῶμα οἱ πολλοί ἐσμεν, οἱ γὰρ πάντες ἐκ τοῦ ἑνὸς ἄρτου μετέχομεν.

verses.restored: See Israel according to flesh: are not those eating the sacrifices sharers of the altar?

familiar.text: Behold Israel after the flesh: are not they which eat of the sacrifices partakers of the altar?

modern.text: Consider the people of Israel: Are not those who eat the sacrifices fellow partakers in the altar?

original.text: βλέπετε τὸν Ἰσραὴλ κατὰ σάρκα· ⸀οὐχ οἱ ἐσθίοντες τὰς θυσίας κοινωνοὶ τοῦ θυσιαστηρίου εἰσίν;

verses.restored: What then do I say? That idol-offering is anything, or that an idol is anything?

familiar.text: What say I then? that the idol is any thing, or that which is offered in sacrifice to idols is any thing?

modern.text: Am I suggesting, then, that food sacrificed to an idol is anything, or that an idol is anything?

original.text: τί οὖν φημι; ὅτι ⸂εἰδωλόθυτόν τί ἐστιν, ἢ ὅτι εἴδωλόν⸃ τί ἐστιν;

verses.restored: No, but that what the nations sacrifice, they sacrifice to daimonia and not to the Divine; I do not want you to become sharers with daimonia.

familiar.text: But I say, that the things which the Gentiles sacrifice, they sacrifice to devils, and not to God: and I would not that ye should have fellowship with devils.

modern.text: No, but the sacrifices of pagans are offered to demons, not to God. And I do not want you to be participants with demons.

original.text: ἀλλʼ ὅτι ἃ ⸀θύουσιν, δαιμονίοις ⸂καὶ οὐ θεῷ θύουσιν⸃, οὐ θέλω δὲ ὑμᾶς κοινωνοὺς τῶν δαιμονίων γίνεσθαι.

verses.restored: You are not able to drink the cup of the Lord and the cup of daimonia; you are not able to share the table of the Lord and the table of daimonia.

familiar.text: Ye cannot drink the cup of the Lord, and the cup of devils: ye cannot be partakers of the Lord’s table, and of the table of devils.

modern.text: You cannot drink the cup of the Lord and the cup of demons too; you cannot partake in the table of the Lord and the table of demons too.

original.text: οὐ δύνασθε ποτήριον κυρίου πίνειν καὶ ποτήριον δαιμονίων· οὐ δύνασθε τραπέζης κυρίου μετέχειν καὶ τραπέζης δαιμονίων.

verses.restored: Or do we provoke the Lord to jealousy? Are we stronger than he?

familiar.text: Do we provoke the Lord to jealousy? are we stronger than he?

modern.text: Are we trying to provoke the Lord to jealousy? Are we stronger than He? All to God’s Glory (1 Peter 4:1–11)

original.text: ἢ παραζηλοῦμεν τὸν κύριον; μὴ ἰσχυρότεροι αὐτοῦ ἐσμεν;

verses.restored: All things are permitted, but not all things are beneficial. All things are permitted, but not all things build.

familiar.text: All things are lawful for me, but all things are not expedient: all things are lawful for me, but all things edify not.

modern.text: “Everything is permissible,” but not everything is beneficial. “Everything is permissible,” but not everything is edifying.

original.text: ⸀Πάντα ἔξεστιν· ἀλλʼ οὐ πάντα συμφέρει. ⸁πάντα ἔξεστιν· ἀλλʼ οὐ πάντα οἰκοδομεῖ.

verses.restored: Let no one seek one's own, but that of the other.

familiar.text: Let no man seek his own, but every man another’s wealth.

modern.text: No one should seek his own good, but the good of others.

original.text: μηδεὶς τὸ ἑαυτοῦ ζητείτω ἀλλὰ τὸ τοῦ ⸀ἑτέρου.

verses.restored: Eat everything sold in the meat market, examining nothing because of conscience,

familiar.text: Whatsoever is sold in the shambles, that eat, asking no question for conscience sake:

modern.text: Eat anything sold in the meat market without raising questions of conscience,

original.text: πᾶν τὸ ἐν μακέλλῳ πωλούμενον ἐσθίετε μηδὲν ἀνακρίνοντες διὰ τὴν συνείδησιν,

verses.restored: for the earth is the Lord's and its fullness.

familiar.text: For the earth is the Lord’s, and the fulness thereof.

modern.text: for, “The earth is the Lord’s, and the fullness thereof.”

original.text: τοῦ ⸂κυρίου γὰρ⸃ ἡ γῆ καὶ τὸ πλήρωμα αὐτῆς.

verses.restored: If one of the untrusting invites you and you wish to go, eat everything set before you, examining nothing because of conscience.

familiar.text: If any of them that believe not bid you to a feast, and ye be disposed to go; whatsoever is set before you, eat, asking no question for conscience sake.

modern.text: If an unbeliever invites you to a meal and you want to go, eat anything set before you without raising questions of conscience.

original.text: ⸀εἴ τις καλεῖ ὑμᾶς τῶν ἀπίστων καὶ θέλετε πορεύεσθαι, πᾶν τὸ παρατιθέμενον ὑμῖν ἐσθίετε μηδὲν ἀνακρίνοντες διὰ τὴν συνείδησιν·

verses.restored: But if someone says to you, This is offered in sacrifice, do not eat because of that one who disclosed it and because of conscience.

familiar.text: But if any man say unto you, This is offered in sacrifice unto idols, eat not for his sake that shewed it, and for conscience sake: for the earth is the Lord’s, and the fulness thereof:

modern.text: But if someone tells you, “This food was offered to idols,” then do not eat it, for the sake of the one who told you and for the sake of conscience—

original.text: ἐὰν δέ τις ὑμῖν εἴπῃ· Τοῦτο ⸀ἱερόθυτόν ἐστιν, μὴ ἐσθίετε διʼ ἐκεῖνον τὸν μηνύσαντα καὶ τὴν ⸀συνείδησιν·

verses.restored: I mean not your own conscience, but the other's. For why is my freedom judged by another's conscience?

familiar.text: Conscience, I say, not thine own, but of the other: for why is my liberty judged of another man’s conscience?

modern.text: the other one’s conscience, I mean, not your own. For why should my freedom be determined by someone else’s conscience?

original.text: συνείδησιν δὲ λέγω οὐχὶ τὴν ἑαυτοῦ ἀλλὰ τὴν τοῦ ἑτέρου· ἱνατί γὰρ ἡ ἐλευθερία μου κρίνεται ὑπὸ ἄλλης συνειδήσεως;

verses.restored: If I partake with thanks, why am I blasphemed over what I give thanks for?

familiar.text: For if I by grace be a partaker, why am I evil spoken of for that for which I give thanks?

modern.text: If I partake in the meal with thankfulness, why am I denounced because of that for which I give thanks?

original.text: εἰ ἐγὼ χάριτι μετέχω, τί βλασφημοῦμαι ὑπὲρ οὗ ἐγὼ εὐχαριστῶ;

verses.restored: Therefore, whether you eat or drink or whatever you do, do all into glory of the Divine.

familiar.text: Whether therefore ye eat, or drink, or whatsoever ye do, do all to the glory of God.

modern.text: So whether you eat or drink or whatever you do, do it all to the glory of God.

original.text: Εἴτε οὖν ἐσθίετε εἴτε πίνετε εἴτε τι ποιεῖτε, πάντα εἰς δόξαν θεοῦ ποιεῖτε.

verses.restored: Become without stumbling-block to Judeans and Greeks and the assembly of the Divine,

familiar.text: Give none offence, neither to the Jews, nor to the Gentiles, nor to the church of God:

modern.text: Do not become a stumbling block, whether to Jews or Greeks or the church of God—

original.text: ἀπρόσκοποι ⸂καὶ Ἰουδαίοις γίνεσθε⸃ καὶ Ἕλλησιν καὶ τῇ ἐκκλησίᾳ τοῦ θεοῦ,

verses.restored: just as I also please all in all things, not seeking my own advantage but that of the many, so that they may be saved/healed.

familiar.text: Even as I please all men in all things, not seeking mine own profit, but the profit of many, that they may be saved.

modern.text: as I also try to please everyone in all I do. For I am not seeking my own good, but the good of many, that they may be saved.

original.text: καθὼς κἀγὼ πάντα πᾶσιν ἀρέσκω, μὴ ζητῶν τὸ ἐμαυτοῦ ⸀σύμφορον ἀλλὰ τὸ τῶν πολλῶν, ἵνα σωθῶσιν.

translation_notes: Daimonia is left transliterated to avoid over-systematizing later demonology; the issue is real spiritual participation at rival tables.
The Lord's table creates one body, so liberty must be interpreted by communion and neighbor-love.
